stem: A club has 9 members. A sub-committee of 4 is to be formed. One particular member, Ramesh, must always be included, and another particular member, Suresh, must always be excluded. In how many ways can the sub-committee be formed?

per_option_rationale.rationale: With Ramesh fixed in and Suresh fixed out, the remaining pool is 9 - 2 = 7 members. Need 4 - 1 = 3 more. C(7,3) = 35.
Ignoring both constraints and applying C(9,4) = 126, treating all 9 members as freely choosable without fixing Ramesh in or removing Suresh.
Applying only one constraint correctly: fixing Ramesh in gives C(8,3) = 56, but forgetting to also exclude Suresh from the 8 remaining.

Reducing pool to 7 but still choosing 4 (forgetting Ramesh is already in the slot), giving C(7,4) = 35... wait C(7,4)=35 = C(7,3). Alternate: pool of 8 (excluding Suresh only) choose 3: C(8,3)=56... instead computing C(8,4) = 70 by excluding Suresh from 9 giving 8, then choosing the full 4 without accounting for Ramesh being fixed.

explanation: Apply constraints before counting. Fix Ramesh in: he occupies 1 of the 4 slots, so 3 more are needed. Exclude Suresh: the available pool shrinks from 9 to 7 (remove Ramesh who is fixed and Suresh who is excluded). Choose 3 from the 7 remaining: C(7,3) = 35.

explanation_sections.punchline: Reduce the problem first: 1 slot taken by Ramesh, Suresh removed from pool, so C(7,3) = 35.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify: combination with inclusion/exclusion constraints on specific individuals. Step 1 - fix Ramesh in: slots remaining = 4-1 = 3. Step 2 - remove Suresh and Ramesh from the choosable pool: available = 9-2 = 7. Step 3 - C(7,3) = (7*6*5)/(3*2*1) = 210/6 = 35.
explanation_sections.lesson: When specific people must be in or out, reduce both the slot count and the pool size before forming C(n,r). Missing one constraint is the most common error.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 seconds. Two adjustments to make: pool goes from 9 to 7, slots go from 4 to 3. Trap: option 3 makes only one adjustment.
